newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- firm as economic data soothes.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- firm as economic data soothes.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices were from flat to up 1/4 of a point in early trade on Thursday, reacting to further reports that portrayed an economy capable of growing without pushing up inflation.
A trader, who said prices rose about 1/4 of a point, added "It's the good numbers, the second quarter Gross Domestic Product and the weekly jobless claims," a trader said.
Another trader, who estimated the cash municipal market's rise at about 0.01, said, "Cash is still kind of a little slow out of the gate, the MOB spread is starting to show a little weakness."

Partly due to concerns about refundings, the MOB spread between municipal bond futures and Treasury bond futures traded in Chicago has eased this week. The September municipal bond contracts climbed 11 ticks to 122-13/32, while the September Treasury bond futures gained 14 ticks to 116-26/32.
This left the MOB spread at plus 179 ticks.
While new issues continued to outperform secondary municipal bonds, a potential trouble spot seen for much of this week remained in evidence--unsold balances.
The City & County of Denver, Colorado's Certificates of Participation in early trade had an $18.745 million balance, out of the $39.955 million offering that was sold on Tuesday.
The main gauge of the secondary market, the Standard and Poor's Corp firmed slightly to $1.303 billion from $1.290 billion.
In early pricing activity, E-470 Public Highway Authority $811 million revenues were priced at 5.35 percent in 2026..
Also, $43 million of Michigan State Building Authority revenue bonds were priced at a 4.20 percent yield in 2001.

U.S. first-time jobless claims for the latest week fell to the lowest level in more than 23 years. The data showed claims slipping to 277,000 in the week ended July 26 from 299,000 in the previous week. That undershot Wall Street economists' consensus forecast for 306,000 of claims.
The sharp decline, while suggesting labor markets were tight, largely was attributed to seasonal factors.

The Commerce Department said the second quarter Gross Domestic Product rose 2.2 percent compared to a revised 4.9 percent in the first quarter. Economists surveyed by Reuters had expected a 1.9 percent gain.
Traders noted that business inventories rose a bit. The report showed a rise to $66.8 billion from $63.7 billion in the first quarter.
In the secondary market, Fairfax County, Virginia, Water Authority Revenues of 2029, which pay a five percent coupon, were bid at 5.29 percent, NET, up one basis point.
And Jefferson County, Alabama, Sewer Revenues of 2027, which have a 5-3/4 percent coupon, were bid at 5.27 percent, up one basis point.
